record.paper_title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems
record.original_question: If f is quasi-hyperbolic, can f have no wandering Fatou component?

evidence.quote: Question 22. — If f is quasi-hyperbolic, then is there no wandering Fatou component?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}^2$ be a complex Hénon map, i.e., a finite composition of maps of the form $(x,y)\mapsto(p(x)-ay,x)$ with $p\in\mathbb{C}[x]$ of degree $\geq 2$ and $a\in\mathbb{C}^*$. The Fatou set $F(f)$ is the largest open set on which the iterates $\{f^n\}_{n\geq 0}$ form a normal family, and its connected components are the Fatou components. A Fatou component $U$ is called wandering if $f^n(U)\cap f^m(U)=\emptyset$ for all $n\neq m\geq 0$.

Recall that $f$ is uniformly hyperbolic on its Julia set $J(f)$ if $T_{J(f)}\mathbb{C}^2$ admits a continuous $Df$-invariant splitting $E^s\oplus E^u$ with uniform contraction on $E^s$ and uniform expansion on $E^u$. The map $f$ is called quasi-hyperbolic if there exists a continuous $Df$-invariant splitting $E^s\oplus E^u$ over $J(f)$ such that for every $x\in J(f)$, $\|Df^n|_{E^s_x}\|\to 0$ and $\|Df^{-n}|_{E^u_x}\|\to 0$ as $n\to\infty$ (i.e., hyperbolicity holds pointwise/non-uniformly, in the dominated-splitting sense weakening uniform hyperbolicity).

Question: If $f$ is a quasi-hyperbolic Hénon map, must $f$ have no wandering Fatou component?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in a recent list of open problems on Hénon maps. While Berger–Biebler constructed polynomial automorphisms of $\mathbb{C}^2$ with wandering Fatou components, and several results rule out wandering components in uniformly hyperbolic and in substantially dissipative dominated-splitting settings, no published resolution of the quasi-hyperbolic case appears in the search results. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems
status_evidence.snippet: In the uniformly hyperbolic case, the answers are yes; one asks whether these properties remain true in the quasi-hyperbolic case.
status_evidence.claim: The non-existence of wandering Fatou components for quasi-hyperbolic Hénon maps is listed as an open question.

status_evidence.title: A polynomial automorphism with a wandering Fatou component
status_evidence.snippet: Berger–Biebler construct a polynomial automorphism of C^2 with a wandering Fatou component.
status_evidence.claim: Wandering Fatou components do exist for some polynomial automorphisms of C^2, but not under hyperbolicity assumptions.

status_evidence.title: Classification of invariant Fatou components for dissipative Hénon maps
status_evidence.snippet: For substantially dissipative Hénon maps with dominated splitting on J, Fatou set has only finitely many components, no wandering ones.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results rule out wandering Fatou components in related (dominated-splitting, dissipative) settings.
